ims.r.short.description: Reads a 16-bit value from the byte array. The 2 bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the 16-bit binary representation of an unsigned integer value.
ims.r.short.name: ims.r.short

ims.r.utc.description: Reads a specified amount of bytes from the byte array. The bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
ims.r.utc.name: ims.r.utc
ims.r.utc.syntax: long ims.r.utc( long bytearray  [, long byte.count] )

ims.read.description: Reads a number of bytes from the byte array into a buffer.
ims.read.name: ims.read
ims.read.syntax: long ims.read( ref string buffer , long nrBytes , long bytearray )

ims.rewind.description: Sets the position in byte array to the beginning.
ims.rewind.name: ims.rewind

ims.seek.description: Changes the current position within the byte array.
ims.seek.name: ims.seek
ims.seek.syntax: long ims.seek( long offset , long opt , long bytearray )

ims.setvbaproperties.description: Sets the properties of the Variable Byte Array (VBA).
ims.setvbaproperties.name: ims.setvbaproperties
ims.setvbaproperties.syntax: long ims.setvbaproperties( long bytearray , long increment )

ims.skip.description: Skips forward a number of bytes in the byte array.
ims.skip.name: ims.skip
ims.skip.syntax: long ims.skip( long nrbytes , long bytearray )

ims.spool.line.description: Spools a line and writes it to the byte array. The characters in the line are copied to the byte array until the last non-white character in the line is encountered. After that, the contents of the line is cleared.
ims.spool.line.name: ims.spool.line
ims.spool.line.syntax: long ims.spool.line( ref string line , long bytearray )

ims.tell.description: Returns the current offset within the byte array relative to the begin of the byte array.
ims.tell.name: ims.tell

ims.w.long.description: Writes a 32-bit integer value into the byte array.
ims.w.long.name: ims.w.long
ims.w.long.syntax: long ims.w.long( long value , long bytearray )

ims.w.short.description: Writes a 16-bit integer value into the byte array.
ims.w.short.name: ims.w.short
ims.w.short.syntax: long ims.w.short( long value , long bytearray )

ims.w.utc.description: Writes an integer value into the byte array.
ims.w.utc.name: ims.w.utc
ims.w.utc.syntax: long ims.w.utc( long value , long bytearray  [, long byte.count] )

ims.write.description: Appends a given number of bytes from the buffer into the byte array, beginning at the current position in the byte array.
ims.write.name: ims.write
ims.write.syntax: long ims.write( string buffer , long nrBytes , long bytearray )

in.fips.mode.description: Function to determine whether the bshell runs in FIPS-140-2 compliant mode. This function supports the 3GL/4GL engineer to write FIPS specific compliant code.
in.fips.mode.name: in.fips.mode

inherit.object.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
inherit.object.name: inherit.object
inherit.object.syntax: void inherit.object( long process_nr , long object_id )

input.again.description: After input by a user, this forces the user to input the data again. If there is an input error, it is preferable to use set.input.error() in the check.input subsection for the field.
input.again.name: input.again

input.to.utc.description: This converts a string to a local date or local time based on a format.
input.to.utc.name: input.to.utc
input.to.utc.syntax: domain ttutc input.to.utc( const string value() , const string format() )

inputfield.invisible.description: This hides the specified field(s) completely. In dynamic sessions, associated label and button are also hidden. To hide a particular element of an array field, append the element number (in parentheses) to the field name. For example: "ttadv301.labl(2)".
inputfield.invisible.name: inputfield.invisible

inputfield.password.description: This causes input to the specified field to be displayed as asterisks (*). To specify a particular element of an array field, append the element number (in parentheses) to the field name. For example: "ttadv301.labl(2)".
inputfield.password.name: inputfield.password

inputfield.visible.description: Use this to redisplay one or more fields made invisible by inputfield.invisible(). To redisplay a particular element of an array field, append the element number (in parentheses) to the field name. For example: "ttadv301.labl(2)".
inputfield.visible.name: inputfield.visible

inputstr.to.date.description: This converts a date input string to the number of days since 01-01-0001.
inputstr.to.date.name: inputstr.to.date
inputstr.to.date.syntax: long inputstr.to.date( string inputstr(.) , string format(7) )

inputstr.to.utc.description: This converts the specified local date and time input strings to UTC long format.
inputstr.to.utc.name: inputstr.to.utc
inputstr.to.utc.syntax: domain ttutc inputstr.to.utc( const string date.inputstr() , string date.format(7) , const string time.inputstr() , string time.format(7) )

insch$.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
insch$.name: insch$

insertln$.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
insertln$.name: insertln$

int.description: The function int() performs explicit double to long type conversion.
int.name: int

is.administrator.description: This checks whether or not the user that is running the bshell has administrator rights on the server that the bshell is running. On UNIX systems, the function returns TRUE if the user has root access to the system. On Windows NT systems, the function returns TRUE if the user belongs to the administrator group.
is.administrator.name: is.administrator

is.classic.ui.theme.description: This function returns true if the UI is running in the classic theme.
is.classic.ui.theme.name: is.classic.ui.theme

is.composite.child.description: This function checks whether the current session is running as a composite child session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a composite session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
is.composite.child.name: is.composite.child

is.current.view.personalized.description: This checks whether the current view is a personalized view.
is.current.view.personalized.name: is.current.view.personalized

is.field.invisible.description: This checks whether a specified field is currently visible or invisible. To specify a particular element of an array field, append the element number (in parentheses) to the field name. For example: "ttadv301.labl(2)".
is.field.invisible.name: is.field.invisible

is.field.multi.currency.description: This returns whether a specified field is a multi currency field.
is.field.multi.currency.name: is.field.multi.currency

is.graph.present.description: This function indicates whether there are active graph defined for this session. This function can be used to determine if additional operations/calculations are needed for a graph.
is.graph.present.name: is.graph.present

is.image.changed.description: This function can be used to check whether an image has been changed onto the image field or the image is changed which is not yet saved or discarded.
is.image.changed.name: is.image.changed

is.image.dropped.description: This function can be used to check whether an image has been dropped onto the image field or the image is deleted which is not yet saved or discarded.
is.image.dropped.name: is.image.dropped

is.interactive.graphs.description: This function tells whether the graphs are displayed interactively.
is.interactive.graphs.name: is.interactive.graphs

is.internal.session.graphs.active.description: This function returns whether the graphs are represented by Internal Session Graphs functionality.
is.internal.session.graphs.active.name: is.internal.session.graphs.active

is.landlord.bse.description: This function returns TRUE if the current BSE is a landlord BSE; FALSE otherwise.
is.landlord.bse.name: is.landlord.bse

is.mmt.controller.description: This function checks whether the current session is running as a multi-main table controller session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode or as a controller within a multi-main table session.
is.mmt.controller.name: is.mmt.controller

is.mmt.satellite.description: This function checks whether the current session is running as a multi-main table satellite session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode or as a satellite within a multi-main table session.
is.mmt.satellite.name: is.mmt.satellite

is.modern.ui.theme.description: This function returns true if the UI is running in the modern theme.
is.modern.ui.theme.name: is.modern.ui.theme

is.multi.tenant.enabled.description: Deprecated. This function is deprecated as the name is confusing and it is actually the same as function is.landlord.bse.
is.multi.tenant.enabled.name: is.multi.tenant.enabled

is.multitenant.restriction.applicable.description: This function returns TRUE if the Multi-Tenant restriction is applicable for this environment; FALSE otherwise.
is.multitenant.restriction.applicable.name: is.multitenant.restriction.applicable

is.rbhp.mode.description: This function can be used to check whether this 4GL session is directly started from a Role Based Home Page.
is.rbhp.mode.name: is.rbhp.mode

is.scrolling.active.description: This function tells whether the find.data section is called while scrolling is active.
is.scrolling.active.name: is.scrolling.active

is.tenant.bse.description: This function returns TRUE if the current BSE is a tenant BSE; FALSE otherwise.
is.tenant.bse.name: is.tenant.bse

is.tree.detail.child.description: This function tells whether the current session is running as part of a Tree-Detail session. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a Tree-Detail session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
is.tree.detail.child.name: is.tree.detail.child

is.view.field.description: This function can be used to check whether a field is currently a view field. This is useful when, for example, the view can be personalized and a total line only makes sense with a specific field in the view.
is.view.field.name: is.view.field

is.webpart.session.description: This function checks whether the current session is running as a primary session in a Workspace WebPart. This function can be useful when a session can be run in different modes.
is.webpart.session.name: is.webpart.session

is_kms_encrypted.description: Determines if an encrypted password is encrypted with the KMS encryption function.
is_kms_encrypted.name: is_kms_encrypted

isdigit.description: This function tests whether the supplied string is the textual representation of an integer value.
isdigit.name: isdigit

iso.to.date.description: This converts an ISO 8601 date string to a local date.
iso.to.date.name: iso.to.date

iso.to.utc.description: This converts a string, representing a time in ISO 8601 format into a UTC long value.
iso.to.utc.name: iso.to.utc
iso.to.utc.syntax: domain ttutc iso.to.utc( const string iso.string )

isspace.description: This tests whether the result of string_expr contains only spaces or is empty.
isspace.name: isspace

java.destroy.queue.description: Removes a queue, given the queue id. This will also remove all buckets on that queue!!
java.destroy.queue.name: java.destroy.queue

java.execute.static.application.method.description: Executes a versioned, dynamically loaded, Java method. These Java mehods can also return a (string) value to the 3 GL.
java.execute.static.application.method.name: java.execute.static.application.method
java.execute.static.application.method.syntax: long java.execute.static.application.method( long Handle , ref string JavaReturnValue , string class.name , string method.name  [, void ...] )

java.execute.static.method.async.description: Executes a Java static method, with no return type, within the JavaVM.
java.execute.static.method.async.name: java.execute.static.method.async
java.execute.static.method.async.syntax: long java.execute.static.method.async( string class.name , string method.name  [, void ...] )

java.execute.static.method.sync.description: Executes a Java static method, with no return type, within the JavaVM.
java.execute.static.method.sync.name: java.execute.static.method.sync
java.execute.static.method.sync.syntax: long java.execute.static.method.sync( string class.name , string method.name  [, void ...] )

java.get.bucket.description: Retrieves a bucket from the queue (if available). The message is removed from the queue afterwards.
java.get.bucket.name: java.get.bucket
java.get.bucket.syntax: long java.get.bucket( long Queue.id , ref string body , long length  [, ref string header] )

java.install.listener.description: Installs a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. Whenever a message arrives on the queue specified by queue.id, the 3GL process will be notified by an EVT_CHANNEL_EVENT event. For installation of a listener at the Java side, see the Java IQueueListener interface definition.
java.install.listener.name: java.install.listener
java.install.listener.syntax: long java.install.listener( long Queue.id  [, long become.owner] )

java.load.application.description: Load the most recent version of a Java application and return a handle to be used in subsequent operations. A Java virtual machine (JVM) is started when required (or an existing one is used), see this overview for details.
java.load.application.name: java.load.application

java.lookup.queue.description: Checks whether a queue is still valid and, if so, if the queue contains a message. The message is not removed from the queue.
java.lookup.queue.name: java.lookup.queue
java.lookup.queue.syntax: long java.lookup.queue( long Queue.id  [, ref string header] )

java.new.queue.description: Creates a new queue for buckets. Upon return, the new queue.id is returned, or an error code is presented. NOTE: queues are removed automatically if the process that created it (or the process that called java.install.listener(…) on that queue) is finished !! See also the 3GL function java.install.listener.
java.new.queue.name: java.new.queue

java.put.bucket.description: Places a message onto a queue. The message contains a header (of type string) and a body (which can contain any character).
java.put.bucket.name: java.put.bucket
java.put.bucket.syntax: long java.put.bucket( long Queue.id , string body , long length  [, string header] )

java.uninstall.listener.description: Uninstalls a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. All buckets on this queue will remain available. The listener can only be uninstalled by the process that installed the listener.
java.uninstall.listener.name: java.uninstall.listener

java.unload.application.description: Unloads an application loaded by java.load.application.
java.unload.application.name: java.unload.application

jca.addFunctionArg.description: Adds an argument definition to the specified JCA Function Call definition. Note that the sequence in which the arguments are added to the JCA Function Call must be in accordance with the 3GL function definition that is to be executed.
jca.addFunctionArg.name: jca.addFunctionArg
jca.addFunctionArg.syntax: void jca.addFunctionArg( long i_funcall , const string i_scope , const string i_type , const string i_name  [, long i_size] )

jca.close.description: Closes the JCA Connection of this 3GL process. After this call, a jca.connect must be done again to re-establish a JCA connection.
jca.close.name: jca.close

jca.closeBde.description: Closes the current BDE Manager on the server of the current 3GL process. The BDE Manager will first handle any request it is processing before it closes.
jca.closeBde.name: jca.closeBde

jca.closeServerFile.description: Closes a file on the server. After closing the file, the file handle cannot be used anymore.
jca.closeServerFile.name: jca.closeServerFile

jca.connect.description: Connects the current 3GL process to a bshell using the specified connection parameters. A 3GL process can have one JCA connection at a time.
jca.connect.name: jca.connect
jca.connect.syntax: long jca.connect( const string i_hostname , long i_port , const string i_bse , const string i_osUsername , const string i_password , const string i_bseUsername , const string i_bshellname , const string i_bshellargs , long i_company  [, boolean i_private] )

jca.connectLocal.description: Connects the current 3GL process to a bshell using the specified connection parameters. The bshell is started on the current host, in the current BSE, for the current user.
jca.connectLocal.name: jca.connectLocal
jca.connectLocal.syntax: long jca.connectLocal( const string i_bshellname , const string i_bshellargs , long i_company  [, boolean i_private] )

jca.createFunctionCall.description: Creates a JCA Function Call definition which can be executed by an open BDE Manager. To this Function Call structure, arguments including their values can be added, as required.
jca.createFunctionCall.name: jca.createFunctionCall
jca.createFunctionCall.syntax: long jca.createFunctionCall( const string i_dll , const string i_function , const string i_returntype )

jca.deleteFunctionCall.description: Delete the specified JCA Function Call definition from memory, including all defined arguments with their values, and the return value, if any. The passed identifier is set to 0 on return.
jca.deleteFunctionCall.name: jca.deleteFunctionCall

jca.downloadFile.description: Downloads a file from the server.
jca.downloadFile.name: jca.downloadFile
jca.downloadFile.syntax: long jca.downloadFile( const string i_serverFile , const string i_clientFile )

jca.execFunctionCall.description: Executes the specified JCA Function Call. The function will be executed using the current open JCA Connection and Bde Manager. When the function has executed successfully, the JCA Function Call return value and its output arguments will have been assigned a value, which can then be retrieved with the jca.getFunctionReturnStrValue, jca.getFunctionReturnLngValue, jca.getFunctionReturnDblValue, jca.getFunctionReturnXmlValue and the jca.getFunctionArgStrValue, jca.getFunctionArgLngValue, jca.getFunctionArgDblValue, jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue functions.
jca.execFunctionCall.name: jca.execFunctionCall

jca.getFunctionArgDblValue.description: Retrieves the value of the specified function argument as a double.
jca.getFunctionArgDblValue.name: jca.getFunctionArgDblValue
jca.getFunctionArgDblValue.syntax: double jca.getFunctionArgDblValue( long i_funcall , const string i_name )

jca.getFunctionArgLngValue.description: Retrieves the value of the specified function argument as a long. Use this also for values of type enum and boolean. Do not use this for values that contain an XML node. Instead use jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue for XML nodes.
jca.getFunctionArgLngValue.name: jca.getFunctionArgLngValue
jca.getFunctionArgLngValue.syntax: long jca.getFunctionArgLngValue( long i_funcall , const string i_name )

jca.getFunctionArgStrValue.description: Retrieves the value of the specified function argument as a string.
jca.getFunctionArgStrValue.name: jca.getFunctionArgStrValue
jca.getFunctionArgStrValue.syntax: string jca.getFunctionArgStrValue( long i_funcall , const string i_name )

jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue.description: Retrieves the value of the specified function argument as an XML node.
jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue.name: jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue
jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue.syntax: long jca.getFunctionArgXmlValue( long i_funcall , const string i_name )

jca.getFunctionReturnDblValue.description: Retrieves the return value of the JCA Function Call as a double.
jca.getFunctionReturnDblValue.name: jca.getFunctionReturnDblValue

jca.getFunctionReturnLngValue.description: Retrieves the return value of the JCA Function Call as a long. Use this also for values of type enum and boolean. Do not use this for values that contain an XML node. Instead use jca.getFunctionReturnXmlValue() for XML nodes.
jca.getFunctionReturnLngValue.name: jca.getFunctionReturnLngValue

jca.getFunctionReturnStrValue.description: Retrieves the return value of the JCA Function Call as a string.
jca.getFunctionReturnStrValue.name: jca.getFunctionReturnStrValue

jca.getFunctionReturnXmlValue.description: Retrieves the return value of the JCA Function Call as an XML node.
jca.getFunctionReturnXmlValue.name: jca.getFunctionReturnXmlValue

jca.getLastErrorText.description: Retrieves an english error text (of max. 512 chars) of the last occurred error. The error text contains information about wrong usage of the JCA Client Functionality, or information about an I/O error, like a lost connection with the server.
jca.getLastErrorText.name: jca.getLastErrorText

jca.openBde.description: Opens a BDE Manager on the server for the current 3GL process, using the current JCA Connection. Per 3GL Process one BDE manager can be open at a time.
jca.openBde.name: jca.openBde

jca.openServerFile.description: Opens a file on the server.
jca.openServerFile.name: jca.openServerFile
jca.openServerFile.syntax: long jca.openServerFile( const string i_fileName , long i_openMode , ref long o_fileHandle )

jca.readServerFile.description: Reads a number of bytes from the file on the server.
jca.readServerFile.name: jca.readServerFile
jca.readServerFile.syntax: long jca.readServerFile( long i_fileHandle , long i_numBytesToRead , ref string o_bytes , ref long o_numBytesRead )

jca.setFunctionArgValue.description: Sets the value of a function argument for the specified JCA Function Call definition. This function can be used several times for the same function argument. In that way it is possible to re-use a JCA Function Call definition, only supplying new argument values.
jca.setFunctionArgValue.name: jca.setFunctionArgValue
jca.setFunctionArgValue.syntax: void jca.setFunctionArgValue( long i_funcall , const string i_name , void i_value )

jca.uploadFile.description: Uploads a file to the server.
jca.uploadFile.name: jca.uploadFile
jca.uploadFile.syntax: long jca.uploadFile( const string i_clientFile , const string i_serverFile )

jca.writeServerFile.description: Writes a number of bytes to the file on the server.
jca.writeServerFile.name: jca.writeServerFile
jca.writeServerFile.syntax: long jca.writeServerFile( long i_fileHandle , long i_numBytesToWrite , const string i_bytes , ref long o_numBytesWritten )

job.add.field.description: Save other fields in the jobdata which are not on the form. All form fields are stored in the jobdata with their values at the moment this function is called.

job.add.field.syntax: void job.add.field( string fld_name  [, long fld_element]  [, long fld_type]  [, string fld_descr] )

keyfields.to.object.description: Store the current value of the key fields to the passed key field object.
keyfields.to.object.name: keyfields.to.object

l.expr.name: l.expr

last.window.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
last.window.name: last.window

len.description: This function returns the length in characters (character count) of the supplied string argument.
len.name: len

len.in.bytes.description: This function returns the length in bytes (byte count) of the supplied string argument.
len.in.bytes.name: len.in.bytes

load.byte.name: load.byte

load.double.description: The function load.double() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes, without trying to interpret that sequence of bytes as the encoding of a sequence of characters. Instead, the bytes are interpreted as the encoding of numerical values.

load.double.syntax: double load.double( string record$  [, long swap] )

load.float.description: The function load.float() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes, without trying to interpret that sequence of bytes as the encoding of a sequence of characters. Instead, the bytes are interpreted as the encoding of numerical values.
load.float.name: load.float
load.float.syntax: double load.float( string record$  [, long swap] )

map.set.shapetext.name: map.set.shapetext
map.set.shapetext.syntax: void map.set.shapetext( long rpid , string text )

mark.handler.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
mark.handler.name: mark.handler

mark.occ.description: This marks the specified occurrence with a reverse bar, makes the marked record the current record in the database, and sets the predefined variable actual.occ to the marked occurrence.
mark.occ.name: mark.occ

max.description: This compares the values of the two arguments and returns whichever is the greatest. The arguments can be of type long or double or can contain any numeric expression.
max.name: max
max.syntax: double max( double x , double y )

mb.cast$.description: This function returns a copy of value$. The runtime type of the returned value is 'multibyte string'.
mb.cast$.name: mb.cast$

mb.cast.to.str$.description: This function returns a copy of value$. The runtime type of the returned value is 'single byte string'.
mb.cast.to.str$.name: mb.cast.to.str$

mb.char.description: This function tests whether a specified code point represents a single-byte character, a multibyte character, or something else. It is mainly used in conjunction with the next.event() function, which returns a character as a long value.
mb.char.name: mb.char

mb.char.info.description: This function identifies the character set to which a TSS-encoded character belongs. It returns the character set ID for the first character in the specified string.
mb.char.info.name: mb.char.info

mb.coerce.to.sb.description: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set, assuring that each resulting character is a single byte. By default, the setting of the current user locale (single-byte or multibyte environment) or the installation locale (Unicode environment) determines the character set to which the string is converted. Code features in the string are skipped.
mb.coerce.to.sb.name: mb.coerce.to.sb
mb.coerce.to.sb.syntax: long mb.coerce.to.sb( ref string string$  [, long setid] )

mb.display.description: This function returns that part of a specified string that fits in a specified display space. The substring is equal to the source string if the source string fits in the display space. If one or more characters do not fit in the display space, a ghost character (default is >) is appended to the substring.
mb.display.name: mb.display
mb.display.syntax: long mb.display( string string_expr , ref string substr$ , long space  [, long flags] )

mb.export$.description: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set. Several ASCII characters and TSS-specific characters are converted to ASCII escape sequences.
mb.export$.name: mb.export$
mb.export$.syntax: long mb.export$( ref string target$ , const string source$  [, long setid] )

mb.export.raw.description: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set. This function is very similar to mb.export$(), but in contrast to that function, no escape sequences are used; instead of that, all ASCII characters are passed unmodified and the TSS-specific line drawing characters and code features are replaced by some replacement character.
mb.export.raw.name: mb.export.raw
mb.export.raw.syntax: long mb.export.raw( ref string target$ , const string source$  [, long setid] )

mb.ext.clean$.description: This function replaces characters in a specified string with spaces, if those characters cannot be converted from native format to TSS.
mb.ext.clean$.name: mb.ext.clean$

mb.hasbidi.description: Deprecated. This function is supported for backward compatibility reasons only. As of object TIV level 2200 (specified with the -T option of the compiler) using this function will trigger a compilation error.
mb.hasbidi.name: mb.hasbidi

mb.import$.description: This function converts a string from the external, native character set to the TSS character set. Certain escape sequences in the input are recognized and replaced by their indicated characters.
mb.import$.name: mb.import$
mb.import$.syntax: long mb.import$( ref string target$ , const string source$  [, long setid] )

mb.import.raw.description: This function converts a string from the external, native character set to the TSS character set. This function is very similar to mb.import$(), but in contrast to that function, escape sequences in the input are not recognized and are not replaced by their indicated characters.
mb.import.raw.name: mb.import.raw
mb.import.raw.syntax: long mb.import.raw( ref string target$ , const string source$  [, long setid] )

mb.isbidi.description: This function checks whether the current environment is a bidirectional one.
mb.isbidi.name: mb.isbidi

mb.isbidi.language.description: This function checks whether the specified language is a bidirectional one. To use the function, you must link to the ttdllbidi library. The function checks the flag ‘ %TF@ttaad110.bidi’ in the table ‘%TB@ttaad110’.
mb.isbidi.language.name: mb.isbidi.language

mb.locale.enumerate.description: This function returns information about one specific locale or about all locales.
mb.locale.enumerate.name: mb.locale.enumerate

mb.locale.info.description: This function returns information about the current locale.
mb.locale.info.name: mb.locale.info
mb.locale.info.syntax: string mb.locale.info( long info_flag  [, const string locale_name] )

mb.localename$.description: This function returns the name of the current locale as defined in the file '$bse/lib/user/u<user>'. The file ‘$BSE/lib/tss_localex.x’  (where x.x is the bshell version) contains all locales that the system supports.
mb.localename$.name: mb.localename$

mb.long.to.str$.description: This function returns a single-character string corresponding to the supplied TSS code point.
mb.long.to.str$.name: mb.long.to.str$

mb.nsets.description: This function returns the number of TSS character sets currently defined. This is useful for retrieving character set information using mb.set.info().
mb.nsets.name: mb.nsets

mb.rev$.description: Deprecated. This function is supported for backward compatibility reasons only. As of object TIV level 2200 (specified with the -T option of the compiler) using this function will trigger a compilation error.
mb.rev$.name: mb.rev$
mb.rev$.syntax: string mb.rev$( string string_expr  [, long flags] )

mb.scrpos.description: This function converts a string position to a screen position. Escape sequences and code features are ignored.
mb.scrpos.name: mb.scrpos
mb.scrpos.syntax: long mb.scrpos( string string_value$ , long string_position )

mb.set.info.description: This function returns information about a specified character set.
mb.set.info.name: mb.set.info
mb.set.info.syntax: long mb.set.info( long setid , ref string name , string desc , ref long n_items )

mb.strpos.description: This function converts a screen position to a string position. Escape sequences and code features are ignored.
mb.strpos.name: mb.strpos
mb.strpos.syntax: long mb.strpos( string string_value$ , long screen_position )

mb.tss.clean$.description: This function replaces characters in a specified string with spaces, if those characters cannot be converted from TSS to native format.
mb.tss.clean$.name: mb.tss.clean$

mb.type.description: This function tests whether the runtime type of the supplied value is 'multibyte string' or 'multibyte string array'. It only tests the runtime type of the supplied value, not its contents.
mb.type.name: mb.type

mb.width.description: This function returns the display width of the specified string; that is, the number of positions the string will occupy on the screen.
mb.width.name: mb.width

mess.description: This retrieves a message from the data dictionary and displays it on screen. Using this function makes your program script language independent.
mess.name: mess
mess.syntax: void mess( string messcode , long separate_window  [, void arg ...] )

message.description: This displays the specified message string on screen in a separate window, and waits until the user closes it. This is applicable in case the message mode of the concerning user is set to "Interactive". In case of a "Non-interrupting" message mode, Infor Enterprise Server displays the message strings in a separate "Messages" window without interruption.
message.name: message
message.syntax: void message( string mess_str  [, void arg ...] )

method.is.allowed.description: This is a special hook for handling centralized authorizations. Use it to perform checks that determine whether certain Data Access Methods are permitted for an object. The method argument specifies the method to check.
method.is.allowed.name: method.is.allowed

min.description: This compares the values of the two arguments and returns whichever is the smallest. The arguments can be of type long or double or can contain any numeric expression.
min.name: min
min.syntax: double min( double x , double x )

mkdir.description: This creates the specified directory. You must have write permission in the parent directory to do this. Access permissions for the new directory are set to read, write, and execute for all users.
mkdir.name: mkdir
mkdir.syntax: long mkdir( string path_name$  [, long access_level] )

ml_all_langs.description: This function creates an MLV that has the same value for all data languages.
ml_all_langs.name: ml_all_langs
ml_all_langs.syntax: string ml_all_langs( const string flatmlv , const string language )

ml_check_in_lang.description: This function retrieves the 'check flag' from an MLF for a certain data language. The 'check flag' is set if the base data language changed after the MLV was translated to a non-base data language. The check flag is retrieved for the base data language if the optional argument 'language' is not specified.
ml_check_in_lang.name: ml_check_in_lang
ml_check_in_lang.syntax: boolean ml_check_in_lang( const string mlv  [, const string language] )

ml_get_baselang.description: Returns the base language of the environment.
ml_get_baselang.name: ml_get_baselang

ml_get_datalang.description: Returns the current data language of the user.
ml_get_datalang.name: ml_get_datalang

ml_get_datalang_of_softlang.description: Returns the data language of the specified software language.
ml_get_datalang_of_softlang.name: ml_get_datalang_of_softlang

ml_is_active.description: Tests whether Multi Language support is active on runtime for the current environment.
ml_is_active.name: ml_is_active

ml_lang_of.description: This function retrieves the language code of the value of string 'mlv' in a certain data language. If the string is an MLV which has no translations the language codes of the value in the various data languages will show a fallback.
ml_lang_of.name: ml_lang_of
ml_lang_of.syntax: string ml_lang_of( const string mlv  [, const string language] )

ml_one_lang.description: This function retrieves the value in a specific data language from a string variable.
ml_one_lang.name: ml_one_lang
ml_one_lang.syntax: string ml_one_lang( const string mlv  [, const string language] )

ml_set_datalang.description: Sets a new data language for the user.
ml_set_datalang.name: ml_set_datalang

ml_set_one_lang.description: This function sets the value in string 'mlvsymbol' to the value of 'flatmlv' in one data language (the 'current data language' is used when the argument 'language' is not specified). The value in the other data languages will be preserved.
ml_set_one_lang.name: ml_set_one_lang
ml_set_one_lang.syntax: ml_set_one_lang( ref string mlvsymbol , string flatmlv  [, const string language] )

modify.set.is.allowed.description: You can use these hooks in your UI script to define the conditions under which the specific standard command should become enabled in the UI. The 4GL engine will use these hooks to determine whether the standard commands must be enabled or disabled.
modify.set.is.allowed.name: modify.set.is.allowed

monitor_add_field.description: Adds or replaces a field to an existing monitor event/interval class.
monitor_add_field.name: monitor_add_field
monitor_add_field.syntax: long monitor_add_field( long event_class_id , const string field_name , void field_value )

monitor_add_metric.description: Adds or replaces a metric to an existing monitor event/interval class.
monitor_add_metric.name: monitor_add_metric
monitor_add_metric.syntax: long monitor_add_metric( long event_class_id , const string metric_name , long metric_type )

monitor_add_tag.description: Adds or replaces a tag to an existing monitor event/interval class.
monitor_add_tag.name: monitor_add_tag
monitor_add_tag.syntax: long monitor_add_tag( long event_class_id , const string tag_name , const string tag_value )

monitor_define_event_class.description: Creates a monitor event class. The class will contain the tags as defined in the BSE.
monitor_define_event_class.name: monitor_define_event_class

monitor_event.description: An event will be reported to the monitoring system.
monitor_event.name: monitor_event

monitor_start_interval.description: Start a timer for an interval of the indicated class.
monitor_start_interval.name: monitor_start_interval

monitor_stop_interval.description: An interval event will be reported to the monitoring system.
monitor_stop_interval.name: monitor_stop_interval

move.imagefield.to.grid.description: If an image is added to an overview session it will be displayed in the view area of the session. This function can be used to move the image field from the view area to the grid. Be aware that moving an image to the grid can have a (major) performance impact. For each row the image needs to be retrieved and send to the frontend. An image should only be moved to the grid if having the image for each row directly displayed is a big advantage and the possible performance decrease is not a big issue.
move.imagefield.to.grid.name: move.imagefield.to.grid

move.window.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
move.window.name: move.window
move.window.syntax: void move.window( long col , long row )

mtime.description: This measures the time elapsed since the first mtime() call. The function is common to all processes within the same bshell. That is, when it is called by a process, the result is the number of milliseconds since the function was first called by a process in the same bshell.
mtime.name: mtime

ncrs.is.session.empty.description: This function can be used in a print or a processing session in an init.form section. The function can be used to decide whether the functional default command should be triggered. Possible the default command is another one, than the command that actually trigges the wanted functionality. The function tells whether the session has no fields left, because the selection group has been made invisible.
ncrs.is.session.empty.name: ncrs.is.session.empty

new.window.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
new.window.name: new.window
new.window.syntax: long new.window( long height , long width , long row , long col )

next.event.description: This removes the event at the top of the event queue and stores it in event. If the event queue is empty, the function waits (that is, it is blocked) until an event arrives. To time out the next.event() function, use set.timer()set.timer.
next.event.name: next.event

no.scroll.description: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
no.scroll.name: no.scroll

not.curr.description: This switches the current and previous values of the specified variable. This is considered a value change by the checking mechanism. So if you subsequently call changed(), that function will return TRUE.
not.curr.name: not.curr

not.fixed.description: You can fill a string with or without specifying a start position. If you specify a start position, unused positions in the string are filled with spaces. You can prevent the string from being filled out with spaces by calling not.fixed() before filling the string. Note that, when you assign a new value to the string variable, positions after the new value are not changed.
not.fixed.name: not.fixed

num.to.date.description: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding year, month, and day of the month.
num.to.date.name: num.to.date
num.to.date.syntax: long num.to.date( long dayno , ref long yearno , ref long monthno , ref long month_dayno )

num.to.date$.description: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding date, formatted as a date string. The sequence of day, month, and year in the string depends on the user data settings defined in the data dictionary (default is "YYMMDD"). The separator character used is also defined in the data dictionary (default is '/').
num.to.date$.name: num.to.date$
num.to.date$.syntax: string num.to.date$( long dayno , long mode )

num.to.week.description: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding day of the week, day of the year, and week number of the year.
num.to.week.name: num.to.week
num.to.week.syntax: long num.to.week( long dayno , ref long week_dayno , ref long year_dayno , ref long weekno  [, ref long yearno] )

oauth1_signature.description: This function takes an URL and two sets of parameters that are going to be passed to a webserver, and calculates the OAUTH1 signature of that request, given a secret password (which must be shared with the web service) and a token obtained in a previous step (see OAUTH1 protocol specification on the web for more details).
oauth1_signature.name: oauth1_signature
oauth1_signature.syntax: long oauth1_signature( const string method , const string uri , const string consumer_secret , const string token_secret , ref string signature , long protocol_parameters , [long form_parameters] )

object.to.keyfields.description: Restore the value of the key fields from the passed key field object.
object.to.keyfields.name: object.to.keyfields

occ.independent.stat.fields.description: Occurrence independent means that the values are not based on one or more selected rows in the grid.
occ.independent.stat.fields.name: occ.independent.stat.fields

occ.independent.view.field.description: This defines the specified field as occurrence independent. This means that its value is not stored in one of the records that is shown in the grid. An example is an order total field that is shown in the grid. Another example is a field that is used to filter out records.
occ.independent.view.field.name: occ.independent.view.field

off.change.check.description: This switches off the checking mechanism for the specified variable. Changes to the variable are no longer monitored by the checking mechanism.
off.change.check.name: off.change.check

on.change.check.description: This starts the checking mechanism by setting a checkpoint for the specified variable. The current value of the variable becomes the checkpoint value.
on.change.check.name: on.change.check

on.drop.description: Call back function which is passed in function enable.drop(). This function will be called when a drop event from the associated session arrives. In this function the business logic related to the drop operation must be implemented. In case database table updates are done in this function, the function must also commit the transaction.
on.drop.name: on.drop
on.drop.syntax: void on.drop( long from.pid , long collection , boolean copy )

on.main.table.description: This copies the contents current record of the main table to the record buffer of that table, saves the record, and executes the specified function. After that the saved record buffer is restored. This enables you to perform actions on the record contents without affecting the values in the table.
on.main.table.name: on.main.table

on.old.occ.description: This executes the specified function for the current occurrence, using the old values of the record. The record must have been previously modified.
on.old.occ.name: on.old.occ

on.recall.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL, is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any changes made to the Business Object must be recalled, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook must then publish a Workflow BOD to ION with a request to recall a previous request for approval.
on.recall.name: on.recall

on.reject.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been rejected in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook.
on.reject.name: on.reject

on.set.approved.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been approved in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook.
on.set.approved.name: on.set.approved

on.set.draft.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been approved in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook.
on.set.draft.name: on.set.draft

on.set.recalled.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case a previous request to recall a started Workflow in ION is confirmed, the DBCM layer will execute this hook.
on.set.recalled.name: on.set.recalled

on.submit.description: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL, is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any changes made to the Business Object are submitted, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook must then publish a Workflow BOD to ION with a request for approval.
on.submit.name: on.submit

open.message.description: Use this to create a new mailbox or to connect to an existing mailbox. You must call this function before you can read from or write to the mailbox.
open.message.name: open.message
open.message.syntax: long open.message( long project , string name$ , long action  [, long fast] )

open.url.local.description: This function opens a URL in an (embedded) browser. This function is only supported in WebUI and LN UI.
open.url.local.name: open.url.local
open.url.local.syntax: boolean open.url.local( string url , long mode  [, string dialog.title]  [, string dialog.message]  [, string browser.title]  [, string redir.param]  [, ref long params.node] )

ostype.description: This function returns a long value that indicates the operating system environment. The possible values are:
ostype.name: ostype

par.abort.client.server.description: This function can be used in the client as well in the server. When there are (application) problems in the client or server, an abort message will be sent to the client and all servers. After this function call, all servers are stopped and all communication will be ended.
par.abort.client.server.name: par.abort.client.server

par.client.close.servers.description: This function will close all servers in a group. Normally this call should only be done when all servers are ready, so after a call to par.client.wait.ready(). Closing the servers means that the application servers will terminate.
par.client.close.servers.name: par.client.close.servers

par.client.get.message.description: This function will check whether a message has been sent by one of the servers in the indicated server group. A server process can send a message back to the client with the function: par.server.send.message(). This function will not wait for any messages from a server process.
par.client.get.message.name: par.client.get.message
par.client.get.message.syntax: long par.client.get.message( long group.id , ref string comm.string )

par.client.get.status.description: Returns the current status of the specified server.
par.client.get.status.name: par.client.get.status
par.client.get.status.syntax: long par.client.get.status( long group.id , long server.number , ref long messages )

par.client.running.description: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing client mode. It will be true when function par.init.client.to.server() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
par.client.running.name: par.client.running

par.client.send.message.description: Send a message to the indicated group or application server. When a server.number is passed, the message is sent to that particular server. Otherwise the message is sent to the first server in the group which is ready. This function will wait until the message has been sent to a server. This does however not mean that the message is already processed by this server when this function returns.
par.client.send.message.name: par.client.send.message
par.client.send.message.syntax: boolean par.client.send.message( long group.id  [, string comm.string]  [, long server.number] )

par.client.start.servers.description: This function is used to actually start the application servers (Bshells) for the indicated group.
par.client.start.servers.name: par.client.start.servers
par.client.start.servers.syntax: boolean par.client.start.servers( long group.id  [, long options] )

par.client.wait.ready.description: This function will wait until servers are ready with processing messages. When no group.id and no server.number are specified, this function will wait for all servers in all groups to become ready. When only a group.id is specified, this function will wait for all servers in the specified group to become ready. When both a group.id and a server.number is specified, this function will wait for one specific server to become ready.
par.client.wait.ready.name: par.client.wait.ready

par.get.no.of.server.description: This function will return the number of servers configured for this client session. See the section Parallel Application Processing Configuration.
par.get.no.of.server.name: par.get.no.of.server

par.init.client.to.server.description: This function is used to initialize the client to server communication for one group. Starting the application servers (Bshells) will be done when the function par.client.start.servers() is called.
par.init.client.to.server.name: par.init.client.to.server
par.init.client.to.server.syntax: long par.init.client.to.server( long nr.of.servers , string server.session  [, string support.session] )

par.init.server.to.client.description: This function is used to initialize the communication to the client. This function must be called rather in the beginning of a program which can be started as server. This because of the fact that the client function has a time out time (default 2 minutes) on starting each server (receiving the 'known' command).
par.init.server.to.client.name: par.init.server.to.client
par.init.server.to.client.syntax: boolean par.init.server.to.client( ref long group.number , ref long server.number  [, ref long tot.nr.servers] )

par.server.get.message.description: This function will inform the client that this server is ready and wait for a new message from the client.
par.server.get.message.name: par.server.get.message

par.server.id.description: This function will return the identification of a server within its group. This function can be useful in includes or DLL’s to determine if the session is running in the context of parallel processing.
par.server.id.name: par.server.id

par.server.question.description: This function can be used by a server session to send a question message to the "support" session in the client. The "support" session in the client must use function par.support.get.question() to receive questions from server processes and function par.support.send.answer() to send an answer message to the server. The function par.server.question() waits until an answer message is received from the "support" session.
par.server.question.name: par.server.question
par.server.question.syntax: boolean par.server.question( string question , ref string answer )

par.server.retry.hit.description: This function must be called in a server after a real db.retry.hit() call. When this function is called x times and x = MAX.RETRY-1, this function will do an abort of the client server communication with the abort message "Too many retry hits in server". See section: Database Retries for a further explanation.
par.server.retry.hit.name: par.server.retry.hit

par.server.retry.point.description: This function is used for setting a not real retry point after a db.retry.point (). It must be used together with function par.server.retry.hit(). See section: Database Retries for a further explanation.
par.server.retry.point.name: par.server.retry.point

par.server.running.description: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing server mode. It will be true when function par.init.server.to.client() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
par.server.running.name: par.server.running

par.server.send.message.description: Send a message to the client. This function will return as soon as the message has been sent.
par.server.send.message.name: par.server.send.message

par.support.get.question.description: This function will wait for a question message from any server. When this function returns -1, the support session must end processing and exit.
par.support.get.question.name: par.support.get.question

par.support.init.description: This function is used to initialize the communication for a support session. This function must be called at the start of a session which can be used as a parallel processing support session.
par.support.init.name: par.support.init
par.support.init.syntax: boolean par.support.init( ref long group.number , ref long tot.nr.servers )

par.support.running.description: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing support session mode. It will be true when function par.support.init() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
par.support.running.name: par.support.running

par.support.send.answer.description: Send an answer message to a server session. This function will return as soon as the message has been sent.
par.support.send.answer.name: par.support.send.answer
par.support.send.answer.syntax: boolean par.support.send.answer( string answer , long server.number )

parse_and_exec_function.description: This function is similar to exec_dll_function(). It loads a specified DLL and parses and executes a specified function within that DLL. pipe.clearerr.description: This resets the error and end-of-file indicators on the specified pipe.
pipe.clearerr.name: pipe.clearerr

pipe.read.description: This reads a specified number of bytes from the specified pipe.

sjv.date.description: Indicates a JSON number is expected that contains a date value (expressed in number of days since 0001-01-01). By default, the date is optional (i.e., does not have to appear in the JSON), can also be 0, but may not be null. The following aspects can be specified:
sjv.date.name: sjv.date

sjv.domain.description: Indicates a JSON value is expected that matches that datatype of the given domain. It is validated using the following properties of the domain:
sjv.domain.name: sjv.domain

sjv.double.description: Indicates a JSON number is expected that contains a double value. By default, the double is optional (i.e., does not have to appear in the JSON), can be any value, including 0.0, but may not be null. The following aspects can be specified:
sjv.double.name: sjv.double

sjv.email.description: Can be passed to sjv.string(): indicates the JSON string contains an email address. An email address is considered valid if:
sjv.email.name: sjv.email

sjv.enum.description: Indicates a list of allowed values of a JSON string. Use this if an enum domain cannot be used.
sjv.enum.name: sjv.enum

sjv.length.description: Specifies an exact length in characters (for strings) or an exact number of elements (for arrays).

sjv.string.description: Indicates a JSON string is expected. By default, the string is optional (i.e., it does not have to appear in the JSON), may be of any length, including a length of zero characters (i.e. an empty string), but may not be null. The following aspects can be specified:
sjv.string.name: sjv.string

sjv.tuple.description: Indicates a JSON array is expected with a fixed length and of which the elements can have different types. By default, the array is optional (i.e., it does not have to appear in the JSON), but may not be null. The following aspects can be specified:

sjv.url.name: sjv.url

sjv.utc.description: Indicates a JSON number is expected that contains a UTC value (expressed in seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). By default, the UTC value is optional (i.e., does not have to appear in the JSON), can also be 0 (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC), but may not be null. The following aspects can be specified:
sjv.utc.name: sjv.utc

sjv.uuid.description: Can be passed to sjv.string(): indicates the JSON string contains a UUID, like 963bb6ef-de70-4812-8e4c-10cb1c966c26.
sjv.uuid.name: sjv.uuid

sock.accept.description: A server process uses this to accept a connection request received on a socket created by sock.listen(). The function returns a valid connected socket on which the server process can send data to and receive data from the client process.
sock.accept.name: sock.accept

sock.clearerr.description: This resets the error and end-of-file indicators on the specified socket.
sock.clearerr.name: sock.clearerr

sock.close.name: sock.close
sock.close.syntax: long sock.close( long socket  [, long linger.timeout] )

sock.connect.description: A client process uses this to initiate a socket connection with a specified server. If the server accepts the connection request, the function returns a valid connected socket on which the client process can send data to and receive data from the server process. The function does not return until either there is a valid connection, or the connection request fails, or a specified timeout expires.
sock.connect.name: sock.connect
sock.connect.syntax: long sock.connect( string host.name , string service.name , long timeout )

sock.connect.ssl.description: The sock.connect() call can be used by a client process to connect to a server using a plain TCP/IP socket. This type of connection is non-secure: data transmitted between client and server can be viewed with a sniffer as it traverses the network.
sock.connect.ssl.name: sock.connect.ssl

sock.daemon.connect.description: This function can be used from a process that is started with the x call. On success, it returns the socket that can be used to communicate with the activating process by means of the x and x functions.
sock.daemon.connect.name: sock.daemon.connect

sock.eof.description: This checks the end-of-file indicator on the specified socket. Note that the end-of-file indicator lasts until the socket is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling sock.clearerr().
sock.eof.name: sock.eof

sock.error.description: This checks the error indicator on the specified socket to determine whether an error has occurred when reading or writing to the socket. Note that the error indicator lasts until the socket is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling sock.clearerr().

sock.inherit.description: A process calls this function in order to take over ownership of a specified socket from another process. The socket is removed from the list of open files for the process that originally owned the socket; it is added to the list of open files for the calling process. The socket is automatically closed when the new owner process terminates.
sock.inherit.name: sock.inherit

sock.listen.description: A server calls this function to create a listen socket that it can use to receive TCP/IP connection requests from clients. The new socket is bound to all available interfaces (IP-addresses of the machine), unless the SOCK.LOOPBACK option is used. In case of success, a valid listen socket is returned, that can be used in sock.accept() to accept connection requests. The used IP address family can be IPv4, IPv6 or both, depending on the system and network configuration settings (e.g. DNS, NIC etc.).
sock.listen.name: sock.listen
sock.listen.syntax: long sock.listen( string service.name  [, long options]  [, ref long port] )

sock.listen.ssl.description: The sock.listen() call can be used by a server process to accept connections from a client using a plain TCP/IP socket. This type of connection is non-secure: data transmitted between client and server can be viewed with a sniffer as it traverses the network.
sock.listen.ssl.name: sock.listen.ssl

sock.recv.name: sock.recv

sock.send.description: You use sock.send() to place data in the send buffer of a connected socket. The data is automatically transferred on the socket when the buffer is full. But you can also call to transfer the data on the socket.
sock.send.name: sock.send
